pull.title: sock: align exception monitoring between poll() and select() backends
pull.body:
On non-Linux platforms, `WaitMany` monitors every socket for exceptional conditions, even when we are not looking to read from it. On Linux, it never monitors those.

Monitoring for certain socket events on some platforms but not others is inconsistent and surprising. In this instance it probably means these cases receive less testing as well, since they are ignored on our most well-tested platform.

Fix this issue by only monitoring for exceptional conditions (which is necessary to detect failed connection attempts early on Windows) for sockets we are also waiting to read from.

comments.body:
Just a note to other reviewers: it looks fine to just drop `FD_SET(s, &err);` instead of moving it to under `if (events.requested & RecvEvent)`. We do not expect and do not care about any "exceptional conditions":

from `select(2)`:
>     exceptfds
>            The  file  descriptors  in this set are watched for "exceptional conditions".  For examples of some excep‐
>            tional conditions, see the discussion of POLLPRI in poll(2).

from `poll(2)`:
>      POLLPRI
>            There is some exceptional condition on the file descriptor.  Possibilities include:
>            •  There is out-of-band data on a TCP socket (see tcp(7)).
>            •  A pseudoterminal master in packet mode has seen a state change on the slave (see ioctl_tty(2)).
>            •  A cgroup.events file has been modified (see cgroups(7)).

Also, our `poll()` branch does not do `POLLPRI`.

However! https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/nf-winsock2-select:

> exceptfds:
>    If processing a connect call (nonblocking), connection attempt failed.
>    OOB data is available for reading (only if SO_OOBINLINE is disabled).

So, `FD_SET(s, &err);` is needed on Windows to handle our non-blocking `connect()`s.
